title: Symplectic balls and the symmetric Mahler inequality
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that for every origin-symmetric convex body K in R^n, n >= 2, every symplectic ball of capacity c < 4 embeds into int K x int K°, and its consequence, the symmetric Mahler inequality vol(K) vol(K°) >= 4^n/n!. Polar bodies, support functions and strip bodies; one- and two-forms, the Pfaffian and volume preservation, flows and Moser's method; plurisubharmonic potentials and dd^c; a ball of capacity below pi k from a holomorphic zero of order k; a planar conformal map from the dilogarithm series and a uniform estimate for its horizontal slice integrals; a symplectic realization of the holomorphic domain inside int K x S int K° with S close to pi k/4, rescaling, and polar approximation of general bodies.
prerequisites: linear algebra and multivariable calculus, with the inverse and implicit function theorems (core course Real Analysis II, Lebl, Theorems 8.5.1 and 8.5.6)
complex analysis of one variable (core course Complex Analysis, Lebl's guide, cited by number)
Lebesgue measure, dominated convergence, differentiation under the integral sign, Fubini's theorem and the change of variables formula (core course Measure and Integration, Fremlin, cited by number)

local solutions of ordinary differential equations and their smooth dependence on initial data (programme lesson Local tools for bundles and transport, Theorem 2.1; inverse function theorem, Theorem 1.2)

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Symplectic balls in symmetric polar products' (OpenAI, 22 Sep 2026; build/main.tex and the sections introduction, history, ball, planar, realization, approximation, 55 kB of TeX; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: one- and two-forms are treated in the language of vectors and skew-symmetric matrices, with the derivative of pullbacks along flows (Lemma 2.7) and Cartan's formula for closed two-forms (Lemma 2.5) proved in coordinates; volume preservation is proved through the Pfaffian identity Pf(M^T A M) = det(M) Pf(A); Moser's theorem is stated for primitives gamma_s depending on s, and the deformation of potentials is reparametrized by a smooth step so that the forms stay symplectic on an open time interval; the support-function criterion for inclusions is stated for compact convex sets without interior, as needed in the polar approximation; the arctangent identity behind the planar map is proved through the logarithm on the right half-plane. The upper bound c_G(U_K) <= 4, which rests on Gromov's nonsqueezing theorem, is mentioned and not used; the packing corollary of the manuscript, which uses OpenAI's ball-packing theorem of another family, is not treated. Field state on 17 Oct 2026: no error report and no peer-reviewed confirmation found; OpenAI's repository has a Lean entry for family 087 (lean/docs/087.md) whose description covers the inequality and the width statement; it was not read.
